title: Causal Abstraction Learning for Multi-Modal Grounded Planning

problem.claim: Multimodal embodied agents need to plan over long horizons in visually rich environments using natural language.

gap.claim: Their generalization is brittle when instructions deviate from familiar examples, suggesting reliance on surface imitation rather than structural understanding.

contributions.claim: CALM is a framework that enables planning agents to discover and exploit causal regularities across tasks.

CALM incrementally builds a causal library by abstracting precondition-effect structures from successful executions and refining them through contrastive causal reasoning when execution diverges from expectation.
The learned causal structure acts as a transferable prior that integrates perceptual cues with mechanism-informed knowledge for planning in novel settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CALM generalizes robustly and efficiently to linguistic and perceptual variation without retraining or task-specific heuristics.
Experiments on ALFRED and VirtualHome reportedly demonstrate consistent gains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal embodied agents support long-horizon planning in visually rich environments through natural language.
Generalization remains brittle under unfamiliar task instructions because agents may rely on surface imitation instead of structural understanding.
CALM discovers causal regularities, abstracts execution structure into a causal library, and refines abstractions through contrastive reasoning.
The resulting causal structure provides a transferable planning prior that combines perceptual cues with mechanism-informed knowledge.
The authors report robust and efficient variation handling and consistent gains on ALFRED and VirtualHome.

source_observation.claim: The framework abstracts precondition-effect structure from successful executions and refines it when execution diverges from expectation.

interpretation.claim: Separating stable causal dependencies from incidental context may improve transfer across task and perceptual variation.

application.claim: Grounded planning systems could maintain reusable causal abstractions and update them using contrastive analysis of execution failures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond the reported linguistic, perceptual, ALFRED, and VirtualHome settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the quantitative gains, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details or computational cost of causal library construction and refinement.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
